# Marshall Elliott

## Overview

- **Age:** About fifty years old (in Volume 4)  <sub>[v4 c9 P36](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0036)</sub>
- **Gender:** male  <sub>[v4 c9 P32](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0032), [v4 c9 P36](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0036)</sub>

## Appearance

He is a long-haired, long-bearded man who was considered right down peculiar-looking during the fifteen years he refused to shave or cut his hair. He looked like a Viking of elder days when dancing with Leslie Moore.

_Sources: [v4 c9 P34](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0034), [v4 c9 P36](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0036), [v4 c16 P6](../source/v04-c16.md#nw-v04-c16-p0006), [v4 c16 P11](../source/v04-c16.md#nw-v04-c16-p0011)_

## Personality

Marshall is a witty, intelligent, and well-read man who rivals Captain Jim in telling a good story. He is extremely determined, stubborn, and possesses a bit of a temper. He is fiercely supportive of children and goes into a fury when he hears of a child being ill-used.

_Sources: [v4 c9 P36](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0036), [v4 c16 P6](../source/v04-c16.md#nw-v04-c16-p0006), [v4 c37 P15](../source/v04-c37.md#nw-v04-c37-p0015), [v4 c37 P17](../source/v04-c37.md#nw-v04-c37-p0017), [v5 c8 P8](../source/v05-c08.md#nw-v05-c08-p0008)_

## History

Born into a family of staunch politicians, Marshall Elliott vowed during a bitter general election fifteen years prior that he would not cut his hair or shave until his political party, the Grits, came to power. He faithfully kept his vow for fifteen years despite remaining a bachelor and looking peculiar to strangers. During this time, he spent leisure hours with local friends, such as going cod-fishing with Captain Jim and watching the old year out at the lighthouse, where he sang ballads and danced with Leslie Moore. When the Liberals finally won power, he immediately visited the barber before sunrise to be shaved and get his hair cut. Shortly afterward, he married Miss Cornelia Bryant and lived with her for over thirteen years. He also went over-harbour to investigate the mistreatment of the child Mary Vance by Mrs. Wiley, expressing great fury over her abuse.

_Sources: [v4 c9 P34](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0034), [v4 c9 P36](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0036), [v4 c16 P6](../source/v04-c16.md#nw-v04-c16-p0006), [v4 c16 P9](../source/v04-c16.md#nw-v04-c16-p0009), [v4 c16 P11](../source/v04-c16.md#nw-v04-c16-p0011), [v4 c35 P29](../source/v04-c35.md#nw-v04-c35-p0029), [v5 c1 P0](../source/v05-c01.md#nw-v05-c01-p0000), [v5 c8 P4](../source/v05-c08.md#nw-v05-c08-p0004), [v5 c8 P8](../source/v05-c08.md#nw-v05-c08-p0008)_
